overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve the May 9, May 23, and June 20, 2023 minutes, rejected its timeliness defense, declined a civil penalty, and ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee failed to timely approve minutes of meetings held May 9 through August 1, 2023.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve minutes of its May 9, May 23, and June 20 meetings.

allegations.summary: Complainant requested a sanction for repeat similar violations; the Committee had prior violation findings, but none for untimely minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to find that this violation was intentional and decline to recommend a civil penalty.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance: the Committee must timely approve minutes going forward (the Committee had already approved all outstanding minutes before the determination).
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance, and caution that a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law and may result in a civil penalty of up to $1,000 per violation.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
